# Recent-championship probe (EXPLORATORY)

**Status: EXPLORATORY.** Not pre-registered, not for the Oct 1 abstract; for the full paper (Dec 4) only if confirmed. Every number below is generated by `analysis/recent_probe.py` into `analysis/outputs/recent_probe.json` (this file is rendered by the same script). Several analyses were added after looking at the data (marked *post hoc*); treat them as hypothesis-generating.

Reproduce: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe analysis\recent_probe.py --seed 20260930 --boot 2000 --out analysis/outputs/recent_probe.json --notes notes/recent_probe.md` (after the scratch steps in the last section). Athlete-adjusted RT (`adj`) = RT minus sex/round/event-type effects minus the athlete's BLUP from the same crossed model that gives the repo's championship offsets (reproduced here: WCH2022 -18.4 ms, WCH2025 15.5 ms).

## Bottom line

1. **The 2022 -> 2023 -> 2025 climb is two different things, not one trend.**
   - **WCH2022 (fast)** is a near-uniform shift of the whole distribution, at every start location (100 m straight, 200 m bend, 400 m start incl. relays and combined events), in every round and on every day. 2022 -> 2023, athlete-adjusted: 5th/50th/95th percentile +19.6/+17.6/+12.2 ms; same-athlete panel (n = 68) +15.4 ms [12.3, 18.5], with no excess between-athlete heterogeneity.
   - **WCH2025 (slow)** is confined to the **home-straight start (100 m, 100 mH, 110 mH) on days 1-4 (13-16 Sep)**. Same athletes, 200 m minus straight-start RT at WCH2025: -22.2 ms [-29.0, -15.2] (other championships: -4.5 to 9.2 ms). The same straight start gave normal RTs on days 7-9 (combined events); the 400 m start was +5.3 ms [0.8, 10.0] vs WCH2023 on days 2-5 (same athletes), against +26.0 ms for straight-start athletes. Within those straight-start races RT rises toward the outer lanes: 2.36 ms per lane [1.56, 3.13], lanes 7-9 12.2 ms [8.1, 16.6] slower than lanes 1-5, and the force onset shows the same gradient. It is the largest of the 18 championship x start cells; other cells whose CI excludes 0: WCH2017 200m 2.13 [0.94, 3.35]; WIC2025 straight -0.44 [-0.9, -0.02].
2. **Verdict on the explanations** (details in the synthesis table): 2022 is consistent with a system-wide time-zero/latency or calibration offset (A), not separable from venue-wide conditions (D); collective behavioural caution (B) is disfavoured (uniform shift, same in all rounds, homogeneous across athletes, unrelated to athletes' baseline speed). 2025 carries a **signal-delivery signature at one start installation during one period**: slower, more spread, and lane-dependent, i.e. consistent with a later and/or quieter signal at that start (A and C together, e.g. athletes cued by a more distant or weaker source), and inconsistent with B or with venue-wide D.
3. **Flag.** The WCH2025 location x day x lane pattern is strong (large, within-athlete, internally replicated in RT and force onset, not seen at WCH2025's other starts, and no positive lane gradient at any other championship's straight start), but it was found post hoc. It does not contradict the abstract's headline (athlete-independent variation is large); it sharpens it: WCH2025's +15.5 ms 'championship' offset is carried by one start installation over four days. If used before a confirmatory test it must be labelled exploratory.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| WCH2023->WCH2025 | straight | 17.2 [11.9, 21.0] | 22.5 [19.8, 24.6] | 27.6 [18.5, 33.8] | 10.5 [1.0, 18.2] | 4.65 [1.49, 8.11] |
| WCH2022->WCH2025 | straight | 37.2 [31.7, 41.7] | 41.3 [37.6, 43.5] | 42.3 [32.5, 48.7] | 5.1 [-5.3, 13.1] | 2.71 [-0.7, 6.14] |
| WCH2022->WCH2023 | 200m | 17.4 [11.7, 26.1] | 16.5 [12.1, 19.3] | 7.7 [-0.6, 19.5] | -9.8 [-21.5, 2.7] | -3.82 [-7.02, -0.88] |
| WCH2023->WCH2025 | 200m | 2.4 [-5.8, 8.0] | 3.1 [0.5, 6.2] | 8.8 [-2.9, 15.0] | 6.4 [-6.4, 16.7] | 1.84 [-0.72, 4.53] |
| WCH2022->WCH2025 | 200m | 19.8 [13.2, 26.2] | 19.6 [15.9, 22.1] | 16.4 [6.1, 25.1] | -3.3 [-15.0, 7.1] | -1.98 [-5.21, 1.26] |

- **2022 -> 2023** moved the body of the distribution together: 5th to 75th percentile +16.1 to +19.9 ms, and the 5th moved no more than the median (median minus 5th change -2.1 ms [-5.2, 1.7]). Only the 95th moved less (95th minus 5th change -7.4 ms [-14.3, -0.2]). So the change is not concentrated in the fast tail. Truncation check: adding WCH2022's 4 recorded false starts with RT 0.080-0.099 s back moves the raw 5th percentile from 113.0 to 111.5 ms.
- **2023 -> 2025** is not a uniform shift: the slow tail moved 15.3 ms [7.5, 21.7] more than the fast tail and the SD grew 6.11 ms. Split by start: the 200 m barely changed (median +3.1 ms [0.5, 6.2]); the straight-start events shifted and stretched (5th +17.2, median +22.5, 95th +27.6 ms).
- Reading: a pure time-zero delay predicts equal shifts at all quantiles (closest to 2022 -> 2023); a weaker or more distant signal predicts a shift that grows toward the slow tail (2025 straight-like; lab: RT SD shrinks with loudness); reduced anticipation predicts the fast tail moving more than the median (not seen in either step: the 5th moved as much as the median in 2022 -> 2023 and less in 2023 -> 2025).

## Q2. Lanes (RT and force onset)

Within-race lane slope of athlete-adjusted RT (ms per lane, 95% CI):

| championship | straight | 200 m | force onset, straight | force onset, 200 m |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WCH2015 | 0.16 [-0.42, 0.73] | -0.87 [-1.91, 0.22] | - | - |
| WCH2017 | 0.45 [-0.45, 1.31] | 2.13 [0.94, 3.35] | - | - |
| WCH2019 | 0.37 [-0.4, 1.07] | 0.51 [-0.22, 1.27] | - | - |
| WCH2022 | 0.14 [-0.51, 0.82] | 0.18 [-1.44, 1.84] | 0.17 [-0.5, 0.91] | 0.19 [-1.39, 1.86] |
| WCH2023 | -0.34 [-0.83, 0.2] | -0.54 [-1.4, 0.28] | -1.38 [-2.03, -0.78] | -0.66 [-1.53, 0.11] |
| WCH2025 | 2.36 [1.56, 3.13] | -0.02 [-0.63, 0.64] | 2.34 [1.56, 3.14] | 0.07 [-0.6, 0.79] |
| WIC2024 | -0.37 [-0.86, 0.15] | - | -0.13 [-0.65, 0.39] | - |
| WIC2025 | -0.44 [-0.9, -0.02] | - | -0.55 [-1.17, 0.03] | - |
| OG2020 | -0.02 [-0.61, 0.52] | -0.5 [-1.58, 0.45] | - | - |
| OG2024 | -0.11 [-0.63, 0.38] | 0.17 [-0.49, 0.84] | - | - |

- Straight-start slopes differ across the five force-trace championships (Q = 42.4, df 4, p = 1.38e-08); without WCH2025 they do not (p = 0.512). At the 200 m start the three force-trace championships agree and are near zero (p = 0.571).
- Other cells whose CI excludes 0 (RT): WCH2017 200m 2.13 [0.94, 3.35]; WIC2025 straight -0.44 [-0.9, -0.02]. None is near the WCH2025 straight value.
- WCH2025 straight by event: 100 m 2.6 [1.78, 3.5], 100 mH 3.58 [1.55, 6.01], 110 mH 0.54 [-0.66, 1.7] ms/lane (the 110 mH starts 10 m behind the 100 m line); by round: F 2.81 [-1.27, 6.55], PR 2.55 [2.04, 3.08], R1 1.94 [0.99, 3.03], SF 3.13 [1.99, 4.23]. Raw median RT lanes 1-5 172.0 ms vs lanes 7-9 186.0 ms.
- Detection line minus 5%-force onset by lane at WCH2025 (straight, ms): L1 1.7, L2 -3.6, L3 -3.3, L4 -3.9, L5 -3.8, L6 -3.1, L7 -2.5, L8 -3.5, L9 -2.0. It is flat across lanes 2-9, so the WCH2025 gradient is in when athletes start to push, not in detection. Caveat: at WCH2023 detection minus onset rises in the outer lanes (L1 -4.2, L2 -3.4, L3 -3.8, L4 -3.8, L5 -1.7, L6 -2.2, L7 -1.5, L8 2.0, L9 4.2), which is why WCH2023's force-onset slope is negative while its RT slope is not; the 5%-onset estimator depends on trace shape, so RT slopes are primary.
- A lane gradient that appears at one start, in one period, is what a difference in signal delivery predicts (an extra path of about 1.2 m per lane is about 3.5 ms per lane at 343 m/s if the cue comes from the infield side). A behavioural account would have to explain why it appears only there, since lane draws follow the same seeding rules at every championship.

## Q4. Same athletes and personal history

Panel: 68 athletes with valid starts at all three.

| change | mean (ms, 95% CI) | median | share slower | SD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WCH2022->WCH2023 | 15.4 [12.3, 18.5] | 14.0 | 0.88 | 13.3 |
| WCH2023->WCH2025 | 16.7 [11.6, 21.6] | 16.6 | 0.79 | 21.5 |
| WCH2022->WCH2025 | 32.1 [27.4, 37.1] | 32.0 | 0.94 | 20.9 |

- By WCH2025 start: athletes whose WCH2025 races were all straight-start +26.0 [20.3, 31.5] (n = 42); all 200 m -7.2 [-16.8, 0.8] (n = 14).
- Heterogeneity of within-athlete change (observed variance minus expected noise, as an SD in ms): WCH2015->WCH2017 16.1; WCH2017->WCH2019 8.8; WCH2019->WCH2022 9.6; WCH2022->WCH2023 -5.3; WCH2023->WCH2025 10.5; WCH2022->WCH2025 10.9; OG2020->OG2024 -2.6; WIC2024->WIC2025 -11.0. 2022 -> 2023 shows none (everyone moved together), the lowest of the World Championship pairs. 2023 -> 2025 shows some, as the start-location split implies, but it lies within the range of the reference pairs, so heterogeneity alone does not discriminate.
- Personal history (panel athletes' championships 2015-2025, median 6.0 each): mean deviation from own mean OG2020 -7.4, OG2024 -1.5, WCH2015 14.7, WCH2017 9.8, WCH2019 5.4, WCH2022 -16.2, WCH2023 -0.8, WCH2025 15.9, WIC2024 -6.0, WIC2025 4.0 ms. WCH2025 was the athlete's slowest championship for 60% of them and WCH2022 the fastest for 63% (chance about 18%).
- Were habitual fast starters the ones who slowed after 2022 (a caution prediction: negative r)? Correlation of pre-2022 baseline RT with the 2022 -> 2023 change r = 0.05 [-0.23, 0.33] (n = 46): no evidence, though the CI cannot exclude a modest negative r.
- Diamond League / national histories were not fetched (next step if needed).

## Q5. Start signal from broadcast audio

Local audio (broadcast, audio only): OG2020_straight 11 starts / 5 videos; OG2024_straight 19 starts / 19 videos; WCH2019_straight 17 starts / 8 videos; WCH2022_straight 8 starts / 7 videos; WCH2023_straight 6 starts / 6 videos; WCH2025_200m 18 starts / 2 videos; WCH2025_straight 44 starts / 4 videos. WCH2025 200 m = two WA full-round compilations downloaded for this probe (gitignored). No audio exists locally for WIC2024/WIC2025, the WCH2025 combined events or the 400 m.

| cell | peaks of the average spectrum (Hz, strongest first) | median rise 10-90% (ms) | median -10 dB duration (ms) | median start sound minus 'Set' (dB) | median foreperiod (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OG2020_straight | 800;470;1920;1630 | 44.5 | 76.0 | 8.2 | 1.739 |
| OG2024_straight | 530;800;1620;1920 | 41.5 | 60.0 | 17.2 | 2.003 |
| WCH2019_straight | 530;1490;2440;2240 | 24.0 | 71.0 | 6.35 | 1.947 |
| WCH2022_straight | 1180;1360;540;880 | 11.25 | 27.5 | 13.4 | 1.76 |
| WCH2023_straight | 2440;1010;1490;1950 | 10.75 | 61.0 | 8.6 | 2.145 |
| WCH2025_200m | 1490;1180;650;2270 | 49.75 | 80.5 | 9.6 | 1.965 |
| WCH2025_straight | 1490;1180;2440;2240 | 32.75 | 68.75 | 5.8 | 2.285 |

- **Signal type.** Vendor is distinguishable: the Omega Games' average spectra peak near 0.8 kHz and 1.6-1.9 kHz, the Seiko championships near 1.2-1.5 kHz and 2.2-2.4 kHz; log-spectrum similarity Seiko-Seiko [0.84, 0.96], Seiko-Omega [0.66, 0.8], Omega-Omega 0.89. Within Seiko the peak lists overlap but are not identical (WCH2022 lacks the 1.49 kHz peak in its top four, yet its overall spectrum is among the closest to WCH2019's); with 6-44 starts per championship from different broadcast chains, a change in the Seiko sound can be neither shown nor excluded. WCH2025's straight and 200 m starts used the same sound (similarity 0.95). Rise time and duration vary between videos (microphone distance, reverberation, processing) more than between championships, so they do not identify the signal.
- **Relative level.** In the same host broadcast, the start sound's level relative to the starter's 'Set' was lower at the straight start than at the 200 m start (straight minus 200 m: -3.8 dB [-6.3, -0.6]; medians 5.8 vs 9.6 dB, n = 34/18, Mann-Whitney p = 0.027). This points the same way as a quieter start signal at the straight start, but it depends on where the broadcast microphones sat relative to the loudspeakers, so it is a pointer only.
- **What broadcast audio cannot tell us:** sound pressure level at the blocks (broadcast gain, compression/limiting, codec and mic position are unknown); trigger-to-speaker latency / time zero (no time-zero reference in the audio; the SIS clock is not audible); which loudspeaker (block vs PA) an athlete heard first; per-lane arrival times. The recorded start sound mixes block speakers, PA and reverberation after unknown gain, compression and codec. Feasibility of reconstructing the delivered signal: signal type yes (vendor level), relative timing of commands yes (foreperiods), level and latency at the blocks no.

## Q6. Synthesis

| explanation | WCH2022 (fast) | WCH2025 (slow) | what would decide it |
|---|---|---|---|
| (A) time zero / signal latency | **Consistent**: near-uniform shift at every start, round and day, no lane gradient; same athletes move together | **Consistent only in a lane-dependent form**: a delay common to all blocks would not stretch the distribution or create the outer-lane gradient | per-block arrival time of the start sound relative to the SIS time zero (a reference click at each block), per session |
| (B) collective caution | **Disfavoured**: 5th percentile moved no more than the median, no round dependence, no athlete heterogeneity, unrelated to baseline speed; still fast in the last days (decathlon) | **Disfavoured**: same athletes normal in the 200 m, near-normal at the 400 m start on the same days; straight start normal on days 7-9; lane-dependent | would need athlete-level evidence (e.g. anticipation measures); not supported by these data |
| (C) signal loudness | Weakly disfavoured: 2022 was faster **and** slightly more spread than 2023, the opposite of the louder-is-faster-and-tighter lab pattern | **Consistent**: slower, more spread, lane-dependent; broadcast pointer (start sound weaker relative to 'Set' at the straight start) | SPL of the start sound at each block (calibrated meter), speaker volume settings per lane |
| (D) venue / conditions | Not separable from A (venue-wide); no temperature association within the meet | **Disfavoured** as venue-wide: same stadium and days, other starts normal or near-normal | cross-meet data at the same venues with a measured signal |

**Decisive data:** SIS logs and configuration by session (speaker routing and volume per lane, any change between 16 and 19 Sep 2025 at the home-straight start, trigger-to-speaker latency), per-block signal arrival time and SPL, Seiko's zero-control records, and the officiating high-speed video (movement onset vs the sound; the WA 'Officiating Video Clip' links return HTTP 403). For 2022: a measured time-zero offset or the RT reported for a reference force.

**Worth registering?** The WCH2025 pattern is the one result here strong enough to matter. A confirmatory test needs data not yet examined, e.g. other Seiko meets at the Tokyo National Stadium (Golden Grand Prix) or the WCH2025 officiating video; predictions: straight-start RT slower than the same athletes' 200 m RT, with an outer-lane gradient, only if the same installation and configuration were used.

## Input steps and provenance (all exploratory, `analysis/probe/`)

1. `fetch_extra_events.py WCH2025,WCH2023,WCH2022,WCH2019` then `parse_extra.py`: WA results pages for 400 m, 400 mH, 4x100 m, 4x400 m (URLs and retrieval times in `extra_rt.csv`; pages cached in `wa_pages/`, throttled 3 s).
2. `fetch_combined.py WCH2025,WCH2023,WCH2022,WCH2019`: decathlon 100 m, 400 m, 110 mH and heptathlon 100 mH, 200 m (`combined_rt.csv`).
3. `dl_audio.py NjJAn9hcsv8 AXbIf9u_G70` (WA full-round 200 m compilations, Tokyo 25; audio only, 800K, gitignored), `find_guns_200m.py` (the measurement pipeline's candidate detector), `run_gun_features.py`, `gun_spectra.py`.
4. `analysis/recent_probe.py` (this note). Inputs and hashes are in the JSON (`inputs`, `q3b_extra_events.inputs`, `q5_audio.inputs`).

Limits: the 200 m compilation guns are detector-selected (score >= 44, jump >= 25 dB) without race matching; the audio 'Set' level uses the detector's last speech burst for them. BLUP uncertainty is not propagated in Q1. The Q4 noise variance is approximate. Scratch WA data are not validated against PDFs as the repo's data are.
